More details emailed to ticket purchasers prior to event date. ABOUT THE THEME: This past year has reminded us how deeply our lives are woven together. Across the world, families have endured separation, communities have mourned, and many have searched for peace, comfort, and healing. In times of sorrow, we are reminded that suffering knows no borders---and neither should compassion. Yet even in difficult times, there are moments that draw us closer. Through music, art, tradition, celebration, and remembrance, people gather across cultures and continents to share joy, offer comfort, and dream together. In those moments, the distance between us seems to disappear, revealing the bonds that have always connected us. The same sun rises over each of us. The same moon watches over those we love. The same stars that guided our ancestors continue to shine above us today. Wherever we may stand upon this earth, we are all bajo un mismo cielo --- under one sky. Día de los Muertos reminds us that love knows no borders. Memory belongs to us all. Grief belongs to us all. Hope belongs to us all. When we gather to honor our ancestors, we are reminded that every life leaves behind a story---and every story is worthy of being remembered.

name: Argentine Film Festival Supported by The Miracle Theater Foundation
description: Saturday 24th 5pm CANELONES Argentina. 91m. Dir. Christian Basilis y Ana Laura Gussoni. During their teenage years in Mercedes, Hernán and his friend Chiri stave off boredom by making prank calls to neighbors. One of these calls crosses the line, deceiving a mother into believing her absent son is coming home for dinner; she prepares cannelloni that go uneaten, and some time later, she takes her own life. Saturday 24th 8pm YO, NARCISO Argentina. 95m. Dir. Adrian Suar. The story follows Rocío Flores (Natalia Oreiro), a sociology professor who decides to investigate modern narcissism. For her study, she chooses Máximo Rey (Adrián Suar) a charismatic and egocentric plastic surgeon as her subject. Rocío goes undercover using a false identity, posing as a patient. However, the experiment becomes complicated when Máximo falls in love with her and the situation spirals out of control.
